answer.rationale: Competitor's price cut targets price-sensitive SMB segment. Memory_73 shows targeted discounting acquired cohorts with -12% 30-day retention—unsustainable. Churn conversations doubling signals defensive pricing trap: matching discounts wastes margin on accounts unlikely to renew. Memory_44 demonstrates enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with superior pipeline quality. Instead of competing on price in a destructive race, redirect competitive response effort toward enterprise_sales_assist: reallocate sales resources to accelerate demo requests and enterprise pipeline, shifting portfolio mix toward higher-retention, higher-margin accounts. This preserves margin, leverages proven conversion strength in enterprise segment, and avoids the retention cliff observed in exp_73. Scale as standard_experiment: dedicate sales team to price-sensitive churn conversations to offer sales-assisted demo path rather than discount, measure pipeline quality and 90-day retention. If SMB churn accelerates beyond acceptable threshold, fall back to referral_incentive (memory_57: +2% retention, no acquisition cost spike) for established accounts only. This trades short-term SMB volume defensibility for long-term qualified revenue maximization.
